function.name: observe_map
function.description: Map facts for one agent at this replan, built from keyframe stereo depth: observed free, occupied and unknown cell counts, frontier clusters, keyframes integrated, the agent's estimated position.

function.name: query_uncertainty
function.description: One agent's visual odometry state: frames, keyframes, and seconds since the last keyframe. Few keyframes or a long gap mean a less certain pose.

function.name: query_route
function.description: The egress route for a human responder (0.40 m clearance) on the current map: found or not, length, which exit. Exploration that finds this route serves the mission.

function.name: list_candidates
function.description: Both agents' candidate actions, computed by the deterministic planner: frontier clusters reachable at the agent's clearance, each with cluster id, path length, cluster size (unknown boundary seen: an information proxy), risk in [0,1] with its reason, whether it needs human approval, and the operator's intent at its goal (`directives` covering it, `priority_weight`, `to_directive_m` = distance to the nearest operator region for this agent, 0 inside). Candidate -1 means hold. `classical_choice` is what the classical planner would pick. `current_task` is the goal the agent is driving to now (null if none): when it was chosen, why, the straight-line distance left, and `candidate` = the index that continues it (-1 if it is no longer a candidate). Cluster ids and indices are renumbered every replan; match by goal, not id. `operator_directives` are the operator's standing orders. Do not send both agents to the same cluster when another one is available.

function.name: request_human_approval
function.description: Ask the human operator to approve one agent's candidate whose risk exceeds the autonomous threshold (§23). Blocks until the operator answers or the request times out. Returns the verdict (approved, rejected or timeout) and the approval_id to pass to assign.

function.name: propose_directive
function.description: Propose an operator directive from the operator's words or from what you see: kind is priority_region | keep_out | assign | explore (polygon = [[x,y],...] in metres, the map frame) or hold | release (agent). It takes effect ONLY after a person confirms it in the console; say why in `text`.

function.name: list_hypotheses
function.description: Open hypotheses about where a responder-passable passage lies, anchored to this replan's candidates (`anchors`: agent -> candidate index), with status set ONLY by a deterministic verifier from the observed map (unresolved | supported | confirmed | refuted | expired) and its reason. An unresolved or supported hypothesis is evidence worth seeking: sending an agent to its candidate lets the next map confirm or refute it. Refuted ones are dead ends.

function.name: assign
function.description: The decision: one entry per agent, {agent, candidate (-1 = hold), reason, approval_id (only for a candidate that needed approval), hypothesis_id (optional: the open hypothesis this move tests), evidence_goal (optional, one sentence: what the agent should observe)}. Call exactly once, last.

message.content: Now we need to consider other factors like uncertainty, route, etc. But likely simplest: assign each agent to highest rank candidate that doesn't need approval and avoid same cluster? Agent0 has many candidates; agent1 also. We'll pick rank0 for each. Ensure they aren't same cluster: different obviously. Provide reasons. No approvals needed as risk <0.5 except some higher risk ones needing approval but we avoid them. So assign agent0 candidate0, agent1 candidate0. Reason: highest utility, safe risk, explores unknown frontier. Let's output assign.
